notes: Endpoint: the brief named /v1/completions. On this checkpoint that path answers HTTP 200 with choices[0].text="", finish_reason "stop" and usage.completion_tokens 0 (4 turns, 71.2 s each) because it passes the prompt as a text continuation rather than through the chat template, so tok_s could not be formed from it. The supervisor approved /v1/chat/completions (one user message) for this experiment on 2026-11-11: same engine, same server, same decode loop, and the path the 12-prompt A/B in docs/experiments/dsv41-kvq-2026-11-11/ used. No sample is fabricated and no zero sample is carried.

Both arms produced non-empty text and used the whole 64-token budget (finish_reason "length"), 347 chars baseline and 326 chars trial. The texts are not byte-identical: this record claims nothing about output parity; the 12-prompt A/B (10 of 12 identical) is that evidence, in docs/experiments/dsv41-kvq-2026-11-11/.

The arms ran one after the other, not interleaved. The between-arm difference of the medians is 0.0008 tok/s (0.23%), smaller than the within-arm spread (baseline 0.3513-0.3534, trial 0.3508-0.3538), so the record says no-change; a 3-sample, single-ordering design cannot resolve an effect this small.

tok_s here includes the prefill of the 239 prompt tokens, because it is completion_tokens over the whole HTTP request, as briefed. At ctx 4096 the packed arm's host KV is 6.4 MiB against 36.2 MiB, and neither is the bottleneck at this context, which is what the hypothesis says.
